title: Certified Argo Project Associate (CAPA)
description: Unofficial practice pack for the Certified Argo Project Associate exam. Written from the public CNCF curriculum (Argo Workflows 36%, Argo CD 34%, Argo Rollouts 18%, Argo Events 12%) and the upstream Argo project documentation. Not affiliated with CNCF or the Linux Foundation.

questions.stem: How is Argo Workflows implemented on a Kubernetes cluster?

choices.text: As a Kubernetes CRD (Workflow) reconciled by a controller, where each step runs in its own Pod
As a replacement for the kube-scheduler that schedules batch jobs directly on nodes
As a Helm plugin that renders workflow YAML into Kubernetes Jobs
As an admission webhook that rewrites Deployments into ordered steps

questions.explanation: Argo Workflows is a Kubernetes-native workflow engine. Workflows are defined with a `Workflow` custom resource, and the workflow controller runs each step of the workflow as a container inside a Kubernetes Pod.

questions.stem: Complete the CLI command used to create a Workflow from a local YAML file: `argo ______ hello-world.yaml`
questions.explanation: `argo submit <file>` creates the Workflow resource on the cluster. Common companions are `argo list`, `argo get`, `argo logs`, and `argo watch`.

questions.stem: In Argo Workflows, the `Workflow` resource is both the definition of the work to be done and the record of its execution state.
questions.explanation: The `Workflow` object holds the `spec` (templates, entrypoint) and the controller writes the live `status` (phase, node results, outputs) back into the same object. Reusable definitions without state live in `WorkflowTemplate` resources instead.

questions.stem: A container template writes a file to `/tmp/report.txt`. Which template section makes that file available to later steps as an artifact named `report`?
questions.explanation: Output artifacts are declared under `outputs.artifacts`, giving a name and the container path to save. `outputs.parameters` with `valueFrom.path` captures a file's *contents* as a string parameter rather than as an artifact.

questions.stem: Which two of the following can be configured as an Argo Workflows artifact repository?

choices.text: An S3-compatible object store such as MinIO

questions.explanation: Supported artifact repositories include S3 and S3-compatible stores (MinIO), GCS, Azure Blob Storage, Alibaba OSS, Artifactory, HTTP, Git, and HDFS. etcd and ConfigMaps are not artifact storage back ends.

references.title: Argo Workflows — Configuring Your Artifact Repository

questions.stem: In a `steps` template, step `generate` produces an output artifact `data`. How does a later step `consume` reference it as an input artifact?
questions.explanation: The consuming step passes the artifact via `arguments.artifacts[].from` using the `{{steps.<name>.outputs.artifacts.<artifact>}}` variable; the target template then declares a matching `inputs.artifacts` entry with a `path`. In a DAG the variable is `{{tasks.<name>...}}`.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a `ClusterWorkflowTemplate` from a `WorkflowTemplate`?

choices.text: It is cluster-scoped and can be referenced by Workflows in any namespace
It can only be submitted by cluster administrators
It runs its pods on every node in the cluster
It is stored in etcd while WorkflowTemplates are stored in an artifact repository

questions.explanation: `WorkflowTemplate` is namespaced; `ClusterWorkflowTemplate` is a cluster-scoped equivalent that any namespace can reference (with `clusterScope: true` in `templateRef` or `workflowTemplateRef`).

questions.stem: Which field lets a `Workflow` reuse an entire existing `WorkflowTemplate` (its templates and entrypoint) rather than defining its own templates?
questions.explanation: `spec.workflowTemplateRef.name` points a Workflow at a WorkflowTemplate so it inherits that template's spec. `templateRef` is used *inside* a step or task to call a single template from another WorkflowTemplate.

questions.stem: A `WorkflowTemplate` can be run directly from the CLI with `argo submit --from workflowtemplate/<name>`.
questions.explanation: `argo submit --from workflowtemplate/<name>` (or `clusterworkflowtemplate/<name>`) creates a Workflow from the template, optionally overriding parameters with `-p`.

questions.stem: What does `spec.entrypoint` specify in a Workflow?

choices.text: The name of the template the controller invokes first
The container command to run in every step
The Kubernetes ServiceAccount used by the workflow pods
The Pod on which the workflow controller runs

questions.explanation: `entrypoint` names the template in `spec.templates` that starts the workflow. It can be a leaf template (container, script) or an orchestration template (steps, dag).

questions.stem: Which template type lets you write code inline with an `image`, `command`, and a `source` block, and exposes what it prints to stdout as `{{...outputs.result}}`?
questions.explanation: A `script` template is a container template with an inline `source`. Its stdout is captured automatically as the `result` output parameter.

questions.stem: Which two template types orchestrate other templates rather than doing work themselves?
questions.explanation: `steps` and `dag` are template invocators that call other templates. `container`, `script`, `resource`, and `suspend` are template definitions that perform the actual work (or wait).

questions.stem: A template has `retryStrategy: {limit: "3"}` and no `retryPolicy`. Under what condition will the step be retried?

choices.text: Only when the container exits with a non-zero code (failure), up to 3 retries
On any failure or error, up to 3 retries
Only on controller errors such as pod eviction
Never — a `retryPolicy` is required for retries to occur

questions.explanation: The default `retryPolicy` is `OnFailure`, which retries steps whose main container failed. `OnError` retries system errors, and `Always` retries both. `limit` caps the number of retries.

references.title: Argo Workflows — Retrying Failed or Errored Steps

questions.stem: You need a cleanup template to run after a workflow finishes, whether it succeeded or failed. Which field do you set?
questions.explanation: `spec.onExit` names an exit-handler template that always runs at the end of the workflow. Inside it, `{{workflow.status}}` can be used to branch on Succeeded/Failed/Error.

questions.stem: In a `dag` template, which field on a task declares that it must wait for other named tasks to complete?
questions.explanation: `dependencies: [A, B]` lists the tasks that must finish before this task starts. The richer `depends` field allows boolean expressions on task status.

questions.stem: A DAG task uses `depends: "A"` (no result suffix). Which task results of `A` allow the task to run?
questions.explanation: With enhanced depends logic, a bare task name expands to `A.Succeeded || A.Skipped || A.Daemoned`. Use suffixes such as `A.Failed` or `A.Errored` to run on other outcomes.

questions.stem: In a `dag` template, tasks with no declared dependencies are started concurrently.
questions.explanation: The DAG scheduler runs every task as soon as its dependencies are satisfied; tasks with no dependencies are all eligible immediately and run in parallel (subject to `parallelism` limits).

questions.objective: Run Data Processing Jobs with Argo Workflows
questions.stem: A step outputs a JSON list of file names. You want to fan out one task per file. Which loop construct takes that list from a previous step's output?
questions.explanation: `withParam` iterates over a JSON array supplied at runtime (typically another step's output). `withItems` takes a static list in the YAML, and `withSequence` generates a numeric range.

questions.objective: Run Data Processing Jobs with Argo Workflows
questions.stem: What is the purpose of the `data` template type?

choices.text: To list artifact paths from a repository and transform the list with expressions before fan-out processing
To mount a persistent volume shared by all steps
To convert an output parameter into an artifact
To stream logs from all pods into a single artifact

questions.explanation: A `data` template has a `source` (e.g. `artifactPaths` on a bucket prefix) and `transformation` steps using expression syntax (e.g. filter by suffix). The result is emitted as `outputs.result` for use with `withParam`.

references.title: Argo Workflows — Data Sourcing and Transformation

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the GitOps principle Argo CD is built on?

choices.text: The desired application state is declared in a Git repository, and the cluster is continuously reconciled toward it
A CI pipeline pushes manifests to the cluster with `kubectl apply` after every commit
Cluster state is exported to Git nightly so it can be restored after failures
Developers run `helm install` from their workstations against production

questions.explanation: Argo CD treats Git as the source of truth for desired state and pulls/compares that state against the live cluster, reporting drift and (optionally) syncing automatically.

questions.stem: Which three of the following are core Argo CD components?
questions.explanation: Argo CD's core architecture is the API server (UI/CLI/API), the repo server (clones repos and generates manifests), and the application controller (compares live vs. desired state and syncs). EventBus belongs to Argo Events and the rollout controller to Argo Rollouts.

questions.stem: Which Argo CD component clones Git repositories and renders Helm/Kustomize/plain manifests? (short component name)
questions.explanation: The repository server maintains a local cache of Git repositories and generates the Kubernetes manifests that the application controller compares against the cluster.

questions.stem: An Application shows sync status `OutOfSync` but health status `Healthy`. What does this mean?

choices.text: The live resources differ from the manifests in Git, but the running workloads are functioning normally
The Git repository is unreachable, but the pods are running
The last sync failed and pods are crash-looping
The Application has been deleted from Git but not from the cluster

questions.explanation: Sync status compares desired (Git) vs. live state; health status reflects whether resources such as Deployments are progressing/available. The two are independent, so a healthy app can still be out of sync.

questions.stem: An Application has `syncPolicy.automated.prune: true`. A Deployment manifest is removed from the Git repository. What happens?

choices.text: Argo CD deletes the Deployment from the cluster on the next automated sync
The Deployment is left running and marked `OutOfSync` until deleted manually
Argo CD restores the manifest to Git from the live cluster
The Application is marked `Degraded` and syncing stops

questions.explanation: Pruning deletes live resources that are no longer defined in Git. Without `prune: true`, automated sync never deletes resources, and they show as `OutOfSync` (requires pruning).

questions.stem: Someone runs `kubectl scale deployment web --replicas=10` in a cluster managed by Argo CD, but Git says 3 replicas. Which automated sync setting causes Argo CD to revert this change on its own?
questions.explanation: `selfHeal` makes Argo CD sync again whenever the live state drifts from Git, even without a new commit. `prune` only concerns deleted manifests, and `Replace=true` changes how objects are applied.

references.title: Argo CD — Automated Sync Policy (Self Heal)

questions.stem: Which annotation protects a single resource from being deleted by Argo CD pruning, even when the Application has pruning enabled?
questions.explanation: The `Prune=false` sync option on a resource excludes it from pruning. `IgnoreExtraneous` only hides the resource from sync-status calculation, `Skip` hooks exclude a resource from being applied, and sync waves control ordering.

questions.stem: A Namespace must be created before a Deployment in the same Application. Given both resources use the default sync wave, which change enforces the order?

choices.text: Annotate the Deployment with `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"` so it applies after the Namespace in wave 0
Place the Deployment manifest earlier in the directory listing

questions.explanation: Sync waves run in ascending numeric order (default wave is 0), and Argo CD waits for each wave to be healthy before starting the next. A `PostSync` hook would run the Namespace *after* the main sync, which is the wrong direction.

references.title: Argo CD — Sync Phases and Waves

questions.stem: Which two fields are required under `spec.destination` in an Application manifest to identify where manifests are deployed?
questions.explanation: `spec.destination` names the target cluster via `server` URL (e.g. `https://kubernetes.default.svc`) or the registered cluster `name`, plus the target `namespace`. `repoURL` and `path` belong to `spec.source`.

questions.stem: For a Git-based source, which values are valid for `spec.source.targetRevision`?

choices.text: A branch name, a tag, a commit SHA, or `HEAD`
Only semantic version ranges such as `1.2.*`

questions.explanation: Git sources can track a branch, tag, or commit (or `HEAD` for the default branch). Semantic version constraints apply to Helm chart repository sources, not plain Git.

references.title: Argo CD — Tracking and Deployment Strategies

questions.stem: Running `argocd app delete myapp --cascade=false` removes the Application resource but leaves its deployed Kubernetes resources running in the cluster.
questions.explanation: A non-cascading delete removes only the Application object. The default (cascading) delete adds a finalizer so the managed resources are deleted too.

questions.objective: Configure Argo CD with Helm and Kustomize
questions.stem: You deploy a Helm chart with Argo CD and later run `helm list` on the cluster. Why does the release not appear?

choices.text: Argo CD renders charts with `helm template` and applies the output; it does not create Helm release records
Argo CD stores releases in its own Redis rather than in Secrets
`helm list` only shows releases installed with Tiller
The release is hidden until the Application is `Synced`

questions.explanation: Argo CD treats Helm as a templating tool. Rendered manifests are applied and tracked by Argo CD itself, so no Helm release metadata exists and `helm list` shows nothing.

questions.objective: Configure Argo CD with Helm and Kustomize
questions.stem: Which Application field overrides a single Helm value, for example `image.tag=2.0`, without editing a values file?
questions.explanation: `helm.parameters` is a list of `name`/`value` overrides equivalent to `--set`. `helm.valueFiles` and `helm.values`/`valuesObject` are the other ways to supply values.

references.title: Argo CD — Helm (Values Files and Parameters)

questions.objective: Configure Argo CD with Helm and Kustomize
questions.stem: How does Argo CD decide to treat an Application source directory as a Kustomize application?

choices.text: It finds a `kustomization.yaml`, `kustomization.yml`, or `Kustomization` file in the path
The repository URL must end in `-kustomize`
All directories are treated as Kustomize unless a `Chart.yaml` exists

questions.explanation: Tool detection is automatic: a `Chart.yaml` means Helm, a kustomization file means Kustomize, otherwise plain directory manifests. `spec.source.kustomize` options (e.g. `namePrefix`, `images`) then apply.

questions.stem: What is the "App of Apps" pattern?

choices.text: A parent Application whose source directory contains other Argo CD Application manifests, so syncing the parent creates the children
A single Application that points at multiple Git repositories at once
A Kustomize overlay that merges several Helm charts into one release
An Argo Rollouts strategy for deploying many apps in waves

questions.explanation: In App of Apps, a root Application manages a folder of Application resources, which Argo CD then reconciles in turn. It is commonly used to bootstrap a cluster declaratively.

references.title: Argo CD — Cluster Bootstrapping (App of Apps)

questions.stem: You must deploy the same application to 20 clusters and keep the Application definitions consistent. Which Argo CD resource is designed for this?

choices.text: `ApplicationSet` with a generator (e.g. cluster or list) and an Application template

questions.explanation: ApplicationSet generators (List, Cluster, Git, Matrix, Pull Request, SCM Provider, etc.) produce parameters that are rendered into an Application template, creating one Application per generated item.

questions.stem: By default, how often does Argo CD poll a Git repository to detect new commits, and how can you reduce the delay?

choices.text: Every 3 minutes; configure a Git webhook to notify Argo CD immediately
Every 30 seconds; increase the number of repo-server replicas
Only on manual sync; enable `selfHeal` to start polling
Every 24 hours; set `syncPolicy.automated` to poll continuously

questions.explanation: The default reconciliation timeout (`timeout.reconciliation`) is 180 seconds. Webhooks from GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket etc. trigger a refresh as soon as a push happens.

questions.stem: How does the Argo Rollouts `Rollout` resource relate to a standard Kubernetes `Deployment`?

choices.text: It is a drop-in replacement CRD that manages ReplicaSets itself and adds progressive delivery strategies
It is an annotation added to a Deployment to enable canary releases
It wraps a Deployment in an Argo Workflow that runs the update steps
It is a Service type that splits traffic between two Deployments

questions.explanation: A Rollout has the same pod template semantics as a Deployment but its controller manages ReplicaSets directly, allowing blue-green and canary strategies with pauses, analysis, and traffic shaping.

questions.stem: Complete the kubectl plugin command that manually advances a paused rollout: `kubectl argo rollouts ______ my-rollout`
questions.explanation: `kubectl argo rollouts promote <name>` skips the current pause step (add `--full` to skip all remaining steps). Related commands are `abort`, `retry`, `undo`, and `get rollout --watch`.

questions.stem: You want a Rollout to adopt an existing Deployment's pod template without duplicating it. Which field do you use?
questions.explanation: `workloadRef` lets a Rollout reference a Deployment (apiVersion/kind/name) for its pod template. The alternative migration path is converting the Deployment manifest to `kind: Rollout`.

questions.stem: In a blue-green Rollout, what does `strategy.blueGreen.autoPromotionEnabled: false` do?

choices.text: The new ReplicaSet is brought up behind the preview Service but the active Service is not switched until a user promotes the rollout
The rollout skips creating a preview Service
Traffic is shifted gradually from 0% to 100% over several steps
The old ReplicaSet is deleted immediately after the switch

questions.explanation: Blue-green uses `activeService` and `previewService`. With auto-promotion disabled, the rollout pauses after the preview stack is ready, giving time for testing before the active selector is flipped.

questions.stem: A canary strategy contains the step `- pause: {}` with no duration. What happens when the rollout reaches it?

choices.text: The rollout pauses indefinitely until it is manually promoted
The rollout pauses for a default of 60 seconds
The step is ignored and the rollout continues
The rollout is aborted and rolled back

questions.explanation: A `pause` step without `duration` is an indefinite pause requiring `kubectl argo rollouts promote` (or an API/UI promotion). Adding `duration: 10m` makes it resume automatically.

questions.stem: Which two of the following can Argo Rollouts use as a traffic router to shift precise canary weights?
questions.explanation: Supported traffic routing providers include Istio, NGINX Ingress, AWS ALB, SMI, Traefik, Apache APISIX, and Gateway API. Without a traffic router, canary weight is approximated by scaling ReplicaSets.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between an `AnalysisTemplate` and an `AnalysisRun`?

choices.text: An AnalysisTemplate defines metrics and success criteria; an AnalysisRun is an instance of that template created and executed during a rollout
An AnalysisRun defines the metrics; an AnalysisTemplate stores the historical results
They are aliases for the same CRD in different API versions
AnalysisTemplates are cluster-scoped while AnalysisRuns are Argo Workflows

questions.explanation: The template is reusable and parameterizable; each rollout step (or background analysis) instantiates an AnalysisRun, which queries providers (Prometheus, Datadog, Kubernetes Job, web, etc.) and records measurements.

questions.stem: A Prometheus metric in an AnalysisTemplate has `successCondition: result[0] >= 0.95` and `failureLimit: 2`. During a canary the AnalysisRun fails. What does the Rollout controller do?

choices.text: Aborts the rollout, scaling the canary down so the stable version serves all traffic
Pauses the rollout and waits for manual promotion
Retries the entire rollout from the first step
Deletes the stable ReplicaSet and keeps the canary

questions.explanation: A failed (or errored beyond limits) AnalysisRun causes the rollout to abort: traffic weight returns to the stable ReplicaSet and the Rollout reports `Degraded` until retried or a new revision is pushed.

questions.stem: You want analysis to run continuously in the background alongside the canary steps rather than as a discrete step. Where do you configure it?

choices.text: `strategy.canary.analysis`, optionally with `startingStep` to delay when it begins
In a separate `Experiment` resource referenced by the Rollout

questions.explanation: Background analysis is set at `strategy.canary.analysis` and runs for the duration of the rollout (from `startingStep`). In-line `analysis` steps run at a specific point and block progression until they finish.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of Argo Events?

choices.text: To consume events from external sources (webhooks, message queues, cloud storage, etc.) and trigger Kubernetes actions such as creating Workflows
To replace Kubernetes Events with a persistent audit log
To schedule Argo Workflows on a cron timetable
To route HTTP traffic between canary and stable ReplicaSets

questions.explanation: Argo Events is an event-driven automation framework: it ingests events from many sources and, through sensors and triggers, creates or patches Kubernetes objects, submits Argo Workflows, calls HTTP endpoints, and more.

questions.stem: Argo Events can only trigger Argo Workflows; it cannot act on other Kubernetes resources or external systems.
questions.explanation: Triggers include Argo Workflow, generic Kubernetes object (create/patch/delete any resource), HTTP, AWS Lambda, Kafka, NATS, Slack, Argo Rollouts, and custom triggers. Argo Workflows is a common target but not required.

questions.stem: Which Argo Events custom resource defines event dependencies and the triggers to execute when those dependencies are satisfied?
questions.explanation: A `Sensor` lists `dependencies` (which EventSource and event name it waits for, with optional filters) and `triggers` (what to do when the dependencies resolve).

questions.objective: Understand Argo Event Components and Architecture
questions.stem: In the Argo Events architecture, which component sits between EventSources and Sensors and transports events?
questions.explanation: EventSources publish events to the EventBus; Sensors subscribe to the EventBus and fire triggers. The older `Gateway` CRD was removed in favour of EventSource + EventBus.

questions.objective: Understand Argo Event Components and Architecture
questions.stem: Which two of the following are supported EventBus implementations?
questions.explanation: EventBus back ends are NATS (Streaming, deprecated), NATS JetStream, and Kafka. RabbitMQ (AMQP) and Redis exist as *EventSource* types, not as EventBus implementations.

questions.objective: Understand Argo Event Components and Architecture
questions.stem: A webhook EventSource named `github` emits an event called `push`. How does a Sensor declare that it depends on this event?

choices.text: A `dependencies` entry with `eventSourceName: github` and `eventName: push`
An `eventBusName: github-push` at the top of the Sensor spec

questions.explanation: Sensor `dependencies[]` reference an EventSource by name and one of its event names (the key under `spec.<type>` in the EventSource). Optional `filters` narrow which events satisfy the dependency, and `eventBusName` only selects which bus to read from.
